query: How should SOC gains and net N contributions be monetized in partial budgets and used to design performance-based subsidies?

response.query: How should SOC gains and net N contributions be monetized in partial budgets and used to design performance-based subsidies?
response.answer: SOC gains and net N contributions should be monetized using market prices or external valuation methods in partial budgets; performance-based subsidies can then be designed based on these monetized values.

results.title: Federal Register :: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program
results.content: Docket Title | Document ID | Comments || Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Standards for 2026 and 2027, Partial Waiver of 2025 Cellulosic Biofuel Volume Requirement, and Other Changes | [EPA-HQ-OAR-2024-0505-0002](https://www.regulations.gov/document/EPA-HQ-OAR-2024-0505-0002) | [1,986](https://www.regulations.gov/document/EPA-HQ-OAR-2024-0505-0002/comment) |  |. In this action, EPA is proposing the volume targets and applicable percentage standards for cellulosic biofuel, BBD, advanced biofuel, and total renewable fuel for 2026 and 2027.[[1](#footnote-1-p25785)]  We are also proposing a number of regulatory changes, including reducing the number of RINs generated for imported renewable fuel and renewable fuel produced from foreign feedstocks and removing renewable electricity as a qualifying renewable fuel under the RFS program (commonly referred to as eRINs). EPA is requesting comment on multiple aspects of this action, including the proposed volume requirements, our technical analyses supporting those volumes, our proposal to reduce the number of RINs generated for imported renewable fuels and renewable fuels produced from foreign feedstocks, the removal of renewable electricity as a qualifying renewable fuel under RFS program, and the other proposed regulatory amendments.

results.title: [PDF] 2025 Proxy Statement - Robinhood Investors
results.content: Stockholders will vote on three proposals at the annual meeting: • Election to the Board of the ten director nominees named in this proxy statement (Proposal 1); • Approval, on an advisory basis, of the compensation of the Company’s named executive officers (Proposal 2); and • Ratification of the appointment of Ernst & Young LLP as the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2025 (Proposal 3). Pursuant to the Founders’ Voting Agreement, each of the Co-Founders and their related entities that are party to the Founders’ Voting Agreement (including entities made party by joinder, “Founder Affiliates”) agreed, upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein, among other things: • to vote all of their shares of common stock in favor of the election of each Co-Founder to, and against the removal of each Co-Founder from, our Board; • to vote together in the election of other directors generally, subject to deferring to the decision of the NomGov Committee in the event of any disagreement between the Co-Founders; and • to ensure that all of their shares are voted as described above, including causing their shares to be present in person or by proxy for purposes of constituting a quorum at the meeting of stockholders (including at this annual meeting).
